subject: Request: temporary capacity reserve for Brightline pilot
messages:
From: Emma King <emma.king@brightline.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot details and capacity needs

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the Brightline engineering team is excited to move to a 2-week production-like pilot. We ran internal throughput estimates and expect up to ~70 concurrent small ticket requests per second in peak windows (95th pct), with average sequence length ~512 tokens.

Can Redwood hold a short reservation for the first two weeks of July so we don't get preempted during the ramp? We'd like a predictable warm pool and slightly relaxed autoscale (allow burst headroom of 2x) while we validate p99 latency at scale. Procurement will need a short statement of work and an estimate for the extra reserved capacity.

Attached is a short spec and our MAP.

—Emma
Brightline Labs

Attachments: brightline-pilot-specs-v1.pdf (pdf, 96 KB), mutual-action-plan-brightline.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Emma King <emma.king@brightline.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot details and capacity needs — Brightline request

Team — forwarding Brightline's ask. High level: 2-week pilot starting ~2026-07-05, peak ~70 concurrent small requests/s, want 2x burst allowance and a warm reserved pool. Procurement needs cost + SOW.

Asks:
- Jonas: feasibility for a temporary reserved slice + autoscale policy override (soft cap increase) for that window. Any impact to queued jobs or critical customers?
- Aditya: ballpark incremental cost for a 2-week reservation including burst buffer and any surge fees.
- Kimberly: product/SLAs — do we need to set constraints on request size or rate-limiting to protect p99s?

We'll need a short internal approval note to send to their procurement. Please reply with concrete numbers by EOD 6/17 so I can loop procurement.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot details and capacity needs — Brightline request

Laura / Kimberly —

We can provision a transient dedicated slice for the 2026-07-05 -> 2026-07-19 window. Proposed approach:
- Reserve a 2-GPU slot group tuned for low-latency inference (A10G family equivalent) as a warm pool. That should cover baseline throughput with caching.
- Configure a controlled autoscale override: allow burst up to 2x for short windows (max 10 minutes per burst, 6 bursts/day). This prevents long-lasting overcommit.
- Lock eviction priority to low for the slice for the duration; we will set preemption to only occur for P0 infra incidents.

Impacts / trade-offs:
- This will reduce available capacity for soft scheduled experiments in the region; I will list two medium-risk pilots that may need rescheduling.
- We will need an ops runbook to manually scale down if observed p50/p95 cost deviates >30% from estimate.

I can get the allocation put into the reservation system if Aditya signs off on cost and Kimberly approves the product constraints.

Attachments: capacity-plan-draft.txt (text, 4 KB)

—Jonas
Lead Capacity Engineer
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Brightline pilot reserve — cost estimate

Quick cost sketch based on Jonas's config and our July rates:
- 2 x GPU warm slice (A10G equivalent) reserved 14 days: $7,600 (reserved slot baseline)
- Burst buffer (allowing up to 2x for up to 6 bursts/day, network & ephemeral storage overhead): estimated additional $1,200 total for 2 weeks
- Ops margin / monitoring overhead: $400

Total incremental estimate: $9,200 for the 2-week window. This excludes any discounts in the SOW — if Sales wants to offer a promotional credit, we can factor it into the deal.

I'll also note run-rate risk: if Brightline's actual average token output per request doubles vs spec, we should expect +25-40% cost. Recommend a contingency clause in the SOW and a telemetry dashboard to watch tokens and burst minutes.

—Aditya
Revenue Ops Analyst
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Brightline pilot reserve — product constraints and SLA note

Thanks — a couple of product-side asks before we lock this in:
1) Rate limiting: require Brightline to use a scoped API key for the pilot that enforces 80 rps burst limit and a per-client token ceiling of 2,048 tokens to avoid pathological requests.
2) Telemetry: add a small set of eval prompts and a quality check webhook that fails the burst if we see >10% drop in match-rate on the eval set.
3) Fallback: if p99 latency degrades >200ms for 3 consecutive 5-min windows, autoscale should disable burst and route to a cheaper fallback model variant automatically.

If Brightline agrees, we can bake these into the SOW. Jonas — can those constraints be enforced at the reservation level and via policy?

Kimberly Park
Director, Product
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Emma King <emma.king@brightline.com>, procurement@brightline.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity reservation — confirmation and next steps

Emma / Procurement —

Thanks for the spec. Internal approvals are aligned conditionally: we can provision a transient reserved slice for 2026-07-05 -> 2026-07-19 and allow a controlled burst policy (2x bursts, limited duration). Estimated incremental cost: $9,200 for the 2-week window (Aditya).

Product constraints to include in the SOW: scoped API key with 80 rps burst ceiling, per-request token cap (2,048 tokens), telemetry hooks and a quality webhook. If p99 latency exceeds the trigger thresholds, we'll throttle bursts and failover to a fallback model. Jonas will own the allocation and ops runbook; Aditya will include cost line items in the SOW.

Next steps for you:
- Confirm pilot start date (we've tentatively set 2026-07-05).
- Sign and return the short SOW (I'll attach a redline-ready draft).
- Grant our team access to your eval prompt set (secure link) so we can add the quality check.

I'll send a redline SOW and the internal approval note once you confirm dates.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW-draft-brightline-2026-07.pdf (pdf, 12 KB)
